cues.en: Let's say you asked yourself once again when you're trying to communicate your work.
cues.zh: 假設你想傳達工作成果，再次問自己：

cues.en: Who's it for?
cues.zh: 這是給誰看的？

cues.en: And the answer is people outside your team.
cues.zh: 答案是團隊以外的人。

cues.en: So clients, customers, fans, it's also really important after you've asked who's it for to follow up with that other question we talked about.
cues.zh: 例如客戶、顧客、支持者。問過「這是給誰看的」之後，也很重要的是，接著問剛才談過的另一個問題。

cues.en: What do they need to know?
cues.zh: 他們需要知道什麼？

cues.en: And now, again, remember always the line here between these two groups isn't set in stone.
cues.zh: 再次提醒，這兩群人之間的界線並非固定不變。

cues.en: They have overlaps.
cues.zh: 它們有重疊。

cues.en: These exercises were going through only to get you thinking from a perspective of the person you're trying to communicate with.
cues.zh: 我們做這些練習，只是要讓你從溝通對象的角度思考。

cues.en: What do they need to know?
cues.zh: 他們需要知道什麼？

cues.en: Now, I think this one is best explained with a little story that I have.
cues.zh: 我想，用自己的一段小故事來說明最適合。

cues.en: Now I'm at a presentation for a board meeting.
cues.zh: 當時，我在一場董事會會議上做簡報。

cues.en: Once we were there to present our results on a recent software proof of concept to some executives and now being an engineer.
cues.zh: 有一次，我們要向幾位高階主管，報告最近一個軟體概念驗證的成果。身為工程師，

cues.en: My presentation slides were clogged with detailed text, barely large enough to read.
cues.zh: 我的投影片塞滿密密麻麻的文字，字小得幾乎看不清楚。

cues.en: It contained every single detail of the project.
cues.zh: 裡面包含專案的每個細節。

cues.en: The techniques used equations, algorithms, acronyms with no definition.
cues.zh: 用過的技術、公式、演算法，以及沒解釋意思的縮寫。

cues.en: The presentation looked great to other engineers, but caused the executives to squint, lean in and
cues.zh: 其他工程師覺得簡報很棒，但高階主管卻得瞇起眼睛、往前靠，

cues.en: basically ignore everything I was saying to just try and read what was on the slides.
cues.zh: 幾乎完全沒在聽我說什麼，只想看清投影片上的字。

cues.en: But once we made it to the end, a slide with a visual appeared to which I palmed off as basically unnecessary.
cues.zh: 到了最後，出現一張有視覺圖像的投影片，而我原本覺得那張沒什麼必要。

cues.en: Oh, I don't worry about that.
cues.zh: 喔，那個不用太在意。

cues.en: But this immediately sparked the interest of the executives.
cues.zh: 但它立刻引起高階主管的興趣。

cues.en: One of them asked, What's that?
cues.zh: 其中一人問：那是什麼？

cues.en: And we spent the next 45 minutes discussing that one slide in detail on the slide, which to me didn't matter.
cues.zh: 接下來 45 分鐘，我們都在詳細討論那一張投影片，也就是我原本覺得不重要的那張。

cues.en: Now, the lesson here is what you think is important.
cues.zh: 這裡的教訓是，你覺得重要的事，

cues.en: Maybe the opposite to others and what's obvious to you.
cues.zh: 對別人可能正好相反；你覺得理所當然的事，

cues.en: What was obvious to me on this slide, maybe amazing to someone else now, knowing this obvious to you,
cues.zh: 例如那張投影片裡，我覺得很明顯的內容，對別人卻可能很驚人。知道「對你很明顯，

cues.en: but amazing to others, you'll start to realize unless they directly tell you.
cues.zh: 對別人卻很驚人」這點後，你會發現，除非對方直接告訴你，

cues.en: Figuring out what your clients, customers and fans want to know is a challenge.
cues.zh: 否則要弄清楚客戶、顧客和支持者想知道什麼，是一項挑戰。

cues.en: And a solution to this is to ask.
cues.zh: 一個解法就是開口問。

cues.en: So most people have a lot to offer.
cues.zh: 多數人其實有很多東西可以分享。

cues.en: Like in my original presentation, no one was saying anything because I was just trying to read the slides.
cues.zh: 就像我一開始的簡報，沒有人說話，因為大家光是想讀清楚投影片就忙不過來。

cues.en: But once we got to something that sparked their interest, they had a lot to say.
cues.zh: 但一碰到引起興趣的內容，他們就有很多話想說。

cues.en: So remember, most people have a lot to offer but rarely volunteer it.
cues.zh: 所以記住，多數人有很多可分享的東西，卻很少主動提供。

cues.en: Ask if what you're saying is clear.
cues.zh: 問問對方，你說的內容是否清楚。

cues.en: Ask if there is anything else they'd like to see, which is what we were talking about here for 45 minutes.
cues.zh: 問問他們還想看什麼，就像我們當時在那裡談了 45 分鐘一樣。

cues.en: Once I realized, Oh, wait, there is a lot of other things they'd like to see.
cues.zh: 那時我才發現，等等，他們還有很多其他想看的東西。

cues.en: Now, of course, you may get something left of field, things that you're unsure of, and these cases, it's up to you to address them before they become larger issues.
cues.zh: 當然，也可能遇到出乎意料、你不確定的問題。這時，你要在它們變成更大的問題之前處理。

cues.en: Don't forget, sometimes the best answer is I don't know, but I'll figure it out and get back to you.
cues.zh: 別忘了，有時最好的回答是：「我不知道，但我會弄清楚，再回覆你。」

cues.en: Or That's not what we're focused on for now and then bringing it back to what you are focused on.
cues.zh: 或者說：「這不是我們目前的重點。」然後把話題帶回正在處理的重點。

cues.en: So these things are just some of the tricks of the trade that I've picked up over time.
cues.zh: 這些都是我隨著時間學到的一些實務技巧。

cues.en: In the next video, we're going to wrap this all up and put together what we've talked about in the last few videos.
cues.zh: 下一支影片，我們要總結這些內容，把前幾支影片談過的觀念整合起來。
